title: Optimal fidelity estimation when one state is pure via algorithmic Uhlmann transform
abstract: The Uhlmann fidelity ${\rm F}(ρ_0,ρ_1) = {\rm tr}|\sqrt{ρ_0}\sqrt{ρ_1}|$ is one of the most fundamental quantities in quantum information theory for quantifying the closeness between two quantum states. Estimating the Uhlmann fidelity to within additive error $\varepsilon$ requires a number of copies of the states, or queries to their state-preparation circuits, that depends at least linearly on the smaller of the ranks of $ρ_0$ and $ρ_1$. Consequently, this rank dependence disappears when either state is pure, in which case the query and sample complexities depend only polynomially on $1/\varepsilon$. However, the known optimal estimator for ${\rm F}(ρ,|ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|)$ due to Fang and Wang (ESA 2025) requires prior knowledge of which state is pure.   In this work, we remove this mathematically unnecessary prior-knowledge requirement and establish an optimal estimator for ${\rm F}(ρ, |ψ\rangle\!\langleψ|)$ under the sole promise that one of the two states is pure, without knowing which one. Our estimator is obtained by specializing the refined algorithmic Uhlmann transform of Utsumi, Nakata, Wang, and Takagi (2025) to the case where one state is pure. In this setting, the Uhlmann fidelity can be recovered as follows: apply a unitary dilation of ${\rm tr}_{\sf A}(|ψ_0\rangle\!\langleψ_1|)$ (or its inverse) to the reference register $\sf R$ of the purification $|ψ_1\rangle$ (or $|ψ_0\rangle$) on the registers $\sf A$ and $\sf R$, estimate the corresponding square-root amplitude in each case, and take the maximum of the resulting two estimates.
summary: This paper presents an optimal quantum estimator for calculating the Uhlmann fidelity between two quantum states when one of them is known to be pure. By adapting the algorithmic Uhlmann transform, the authors achieve query-optimal complexity $O(1/\varepsilon)$, providing a significant theoretical improvement over general mixed-state estimation protocols.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop an optimal quantum estimator for the Uhlmann fidelity $F(ho_0, ho_1)$ when only the promise that at least one of the two input states ($ho_0$ or $ho_1$) is pure is available.
main_result: The authors establish a query-optimal quantum estimator achieving complexity $\Theta(1/\varepsilon)$, which significantly improves upon previous bounds in this specific scenario.
method: The method involves specializing the refined algorithmic Uhlmann transform to utilize the structure imposed by one pure state, relating the fidelity estimation to estimating maximum square-root amplitudes derived from the unitary dilation of the Uhlmann cross operator.
model_or_system: The system involves two unknown quantum states, $ho_0$ and $ho_1$, whose closeness is quantified by the Uhlmann fidelity. The analysis focuses on accessing these states via state-preparation circuits or receiving multiple copies.
key_observables: Uhlmann fidelity $F(ho_0, ho_1)$, which equals the norm of the Uhlmann cross operator $\lVert X Vert$ when one state is pure.
important_parameters: The estimation precision $\varepsilon$, and the query/sample complexities (e.g., $O(1/\varepsilon)$ queries).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that at least one of the two states ($ho_0$ or $ho_1$) is pure, which simplifies the structure of the Uhlmann cross operator.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Uhlmann cross operator $X$ and its unitary dilation block. Other figures detail quantum circuits used to estimate related quantities $a_0$ and $a_1$.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon existing fidelity estimation techniques, deriving an estimator by specializing the algorithmic Uhlmann transform for the one-pure-state case, culminating in a concrete algorithm (Algorithm 1) for optimal estimation.
why_interesting: This work provides quantum computational tools to estimate fundamental physical quantities like state overlap with high efficiency, which is crucial for characterizing quantum channels or verifying quantum process fidelity.
